Core Validation Report — Pathway A satisfied

I located the relevant material in the uploaded Core Radiology, Second Edition PDF, so Core availability is proven for this run. The primary Core coverage is Genitourinary Imaging, GU 316–318, with the immediately adjacent ovarian-torsion material used for the Doppler pitfall and Obstetrical Imaging, pages 330–331 used for the corpus-luteum-versus-ectopic discriminator.

Core validation digest: Core explicitly teaches follicular, corpus luteal, and theca lutein cysts as the functional-cyst framework; it operationally defines follicular and corpus luteal cysts as >3 cm. A simple cyst is round/oval, anechoic, imperceptibly thin-walled, posteriorly enhancing, and lacks septations, solid components, or internal Doppler flow. Hemorrhagic cyst evolution produces web-like internal echoes and retractile avascular clot; concave avascular clot is contrasted with a convex vascular mural nodule. Core also provides the 2019 SRU follow-up framework and emphasizes that ring-of-fire vascularity is nonspecific because both ectopic pregnancy and corpus luteum may show it.

Whole-source coverage audit completed from full Core pages and full article text.
Core Summary attached; derived from full Core coverage, not from validation digest.
Card generation used full-source review, not digest summary.

Core Summary

Core's central recognition model is: functional cyst subtype → ovarian morphology → hemorrhagic evolution → resolution/follow-up behavior. Follicular cysts arise after failed ovulation; corpus luteal cysts after failed involution; theca lutein cysts occur with elevated hCG states. Hemorrhage most commonly complicates a corpus luteum, with web-like echoes and avascular retractile clot as important sonographic discriminators.

For management, Core's SRU 2019 summary allows no follow-up for a well-characterized premenopausal simple cyst through 7 cm when visualization/confidence is superior, while larger or incompletely characterized lesions receive follow-up. Hemorrhagic cysts >5 cm receive short-interval ultrasound to document resolution.

For the critical ectopic mimic, Core states that ring-of-fire flow is not specific. The key discriminator is intraovarian versus extraovarian location; a separate tubal/adnexal ring in the absence of an IUP has >95% PPV for ectopic pregnancy.

Whole-source synthesis audit

The final deck uses Core + RadPrimer + STATdx synthesis. Definitions, ultrasound appearance, differential logic, pathology/mechanism, the subtype framework, and management are represented in both Core and the article package. CT appearance, MR appearance, O-RADS 2022 details, rupture/free-fluid examples, large-cyst examples, and the expanded vascular-margin pitfalls are article additions. Nuclear medicine appearance is absent from both and was therefore not invented.

Two important source differences were preserved rather than silently reconciled. Core uses >3 cm as the general follicular-cyst threshold, while STATdx image 10 explicitly labels a 2.55 cm dominant cystic structure during ovarian suppression as a follicular cyst; that case-specific diagnosis remains intact while the definition card follows Core's general threshold. Also, Core's SRU wording for a confidently characterized >5–7 cm premenopausal simple cyst differs slightly from the RadPrimer summary; the dedicated SRU card follows Core because Core is first in the requested hierarchy, while the RadPrimer/STATdx nuances remain in the shared summary and O-RADS cards.

STATdx images 1–4 remain excluded because the supplied master registry explicitly identifies them as exact duplicates of RadPrimer images 1–4.
